prompt: Maya makes granola. One batch uses $\frac{2}{3}$ cup of oats. How many cups of oats does she need for $3$ batches?
hint: Every batch uses the same amount of oats. Three equal amounts can be found by adding repeatedly or by multiplying.

hints.text: Every batch uses the same amount of oats. Three equal amounts can be found by adding repeatedly or by multiplying.
Work out $3 \times \frac{2}{3}$. The whole number multiplies the numerator while the denominator stays the same, giving a number of thirds.
$3 \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{6}{3} = 2$, so Maya needs $2$ cups of oats.

explanation: Three batches each use $\frac{2}{3}$ cup, so the total is $3 \times \frac{2}{3}$.
A whole number times a fraction multiplies the numerator, because it counts more pieces of the same size: $3 \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{6}{3}$.
The fraction $\frac{6}{3}$ means $6 \div 3$, and that equals $2$.
Maya needs $2$ cups of oats for three batches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just add them up
steps: Three thirds make one whole, so six thirds make $2$ wholes.
